subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Maths simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Find the mean of 6, 6, 10, 4, 4.
Find the median of 14, 3, 9, 21, 6, 18.
questions.explain: Order: 3, 6, 9, 14, 18, 21. Middle two are 9 and 14; median = (9 + 14)/2 = 11.5.

questions.q: A data set has mean 12 for 6 values. What is the total of all values?
Number of pets: 0 (freq 6), 1 (freq 9), 2 (freq 5). Find the mean number of pets.
Scores 5 (freq 4), 10 (freq 6), 15 (freq 10). Find the mean.
Groups: 0-10 (freq 2, mid 5), 10-20 (freq 5, mid 15), 20-30 (freq 3, mid 25). Estimate the mean.
In grouped data, which class contains the median if it lies in the 10th of 20 ordered values?
options: The class where cumulative frequency first reaches or passes 10
The class with the highest frequency
questions.explain: The median class is the one in which the cumulative frequency first reaches the median position (here the 10th value).

questions.q: Which of these is a disadvantage of a small sample?
options: It may not represent the whole population well
questions.explain: Small samples are more likely to be unrepresentative and give unreliable estimates.

questions.q: A club has 400 members. A stratified sample of 40 is taken; 120 members are juniors. How many juniors in the sample?
A bar chart shows 8, 12, 5 and 15 for four categories. What is the total frequency?
In a pie chart of 120 people, one sector is 90°. How many people does it represent?
A class 20-30 has frequency 24. Find its frequency density.
A histogram bar has frequency density 3.5 over a class of width 4. Find its frequency.
A box plot shows Q1 = 18 and Q3 = 27. Find the interquartile range.
For 60 data values on a cumulative frequency graph, the lower quartile is read at which cumulative frequency?
questions.explain: The lower quartile Q1 is at n/4 = 60/4 = 15.

questions.q: Points on a scatter graph are scattered with no pattern. What correlation is shown?
questions.explain: If the points show no clear trend, there is no correlation between the variables.

questions.q: Which point should a line of best fit ideally pass close to?
options: The mean point (mean of x, mean of y)
questions.explain: A good line of best fit passes through the mean point and balances the points either side.

questions.q: Temperature and ice cream sales show strong positive correlation. This means as temperature rises, sales tend to what?
questions.explain: Positive correlation means the two variables increase together, so sales tend to rise with temperature.

questions.q: Team X scores mean 20 range 6; Team Y scores mean 20 range 14. Which team is more consistent?
options: Team Y, because its range is larger
Team X, because its mean is higher
Team X, because its range is smaller
questions.explain: Same mean, but a smaller range means less variation, so Team X is more consistent.

questions.q: To compare two distributions fully, you should compare an average and what else?
questions.explain: A full comparison needs both an average (median/mean) and a measure of spread (range/IQR).
